[LNAM.2.6.1] **Letters versus controls — the load-bearing distinction.** "Bidi"
names two disjoint things: strong right-to-left **letters** (Arabic, Hebrew, … —
ordinary script letters with inherent directionality) and bidi **control
characters** (invisible format codepoints `U+202A`–`202E`, `U+2066`–`2069`,
`U+200E`/`200F`, `U+061C`). The rules in this section constrain **only the control
characters.** Strong RTL letters are ordinary identifier ([LNAM.2.2]) and string
([LNAM.2.7]) characters and are unrestricted: **`schema مستشعر:` is legal**, and its
display ordering is produced by the implicit Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm (UAX #9)
with no control characters required.
